name: Strategic Planning and Scenarios
title: Strategic Planning and Scenarios
answer: A strategic plan for AI gives a district a clear direction by naming goals tied to student learning and staff time, the rules for AI use, the pilots underway, and how results will be measured. Leaders and the community must set the goals and priorities, because a plan written mostly by a tool will not guide real decisions. Scenario planning and crisis communication planning help the district prepare for vendor failures, new restrictions, data breaches, and AI related incidents.

sections.body: This idea is about giving a district a clear direction for AI through a strategic plan, and about preparing for an uncertain future through scenario planning. The plan should name goals tied to student learning and staff time, the rules that govern AI use, the pilots underway, and how results will be measured. AI can help draft sections of the plan, but the goals and priorities must come from the district's leaders and community. A plan written mostly by a tool will not guide real decisions. Scenario planning addresses the problem of uncertainty by asking what happens if a major vendor fails, if new laws restrict certain uses of AI, or if a data breach exposes student information.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or district, leaders and the community set the goals and priorities, while AI may be used to help draft sections of the plan. The plan itself names goals tied to student learning and staff time, the rules that govern AI use, the pilots underway, and how results will be measured. Leaders then talk through scenarios in advance, such as a major vendor failing, new laws restricting certain uses of AI, or a data breach exposing student information. Crisis communication plans should include AI related scenarios, such as a deepfake of a staff member, a chatbot giving harmful advice to a student, or a breach at an AI vendor. Prepared templates, reviewed in advance, make fast and honest communication possible in those situations.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no research evidence for strategic planning and scenario planning. It refers to the Los Angeles case (EdSurge, 2024) as an example of a major vendor failing, but it does not state a study or finding from it. This idea therefore rests on practice and on the principles from Chapter 14 rather than on research presented here.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The goals and priorities must come from the district's leaders and community, not from a tool, because a plan written mostly by a tool will not guide real decisions. AI may help draft sections of the plan, but that drafting role is limited. Scenario planning and crisis communication planning are meant to make the district more resilient, and the text says the principles from Chapter 14 apply to AI related crisis communication. The decisions about goals, priorities, rules, and how to respond to a deepfake, harmful chatbot advice, or a vendor breach stay with people.
